evidence_strength: Recorded as a session instruction typed by the owner during a goal round. It is NOT a get_goal artifact and must not be described as one. It stands beside OWNER_AUTHORIZATION_RDCJT_001.json and OWNER_AUTHORIZATION_RDCJT_002.json, which it neither replaces nor weakens.

why_a_third_record_exists.summary: RDCJT_002 declared bounds.jobs = 2. BOTH slots were consumed by infrastructure failures that produced NO measurement, so this record authorises the two real runs it was written for. This is stated explicitly rather than resolved by editing RDCJT_002, because editing that record would change its sha256, orphan the two receipts that already bind to the old digest, and quietly erase the evidence that the failures happened.

slot_1.money_moved: NONE. Refused before the reservation. Ledger unchanged at revision 69, 71 reservations.

slot_2.where: aws/budget.py publish -> read_locked, after the write-ahead history record was already committed
slot_2.money_moved: A $7.00 RESERVATION was recorded in the ledger (revision 70) and NOTHING WAS LAUNCHED. No EC2 instance was created, so the real AWS charge for this attempt is approximately zero. The reservation is not refunded: the policy is RESERVED_NO_AUTOMATIC_REFUND, and it remains in the ledger under that job name.

orphaned_reservation.why_not: reserve_budget refuses a job name that already holds a reservation (JOB_ALREADY_RESERVED_NO_AUTOMATIC_RETRY), and unlike a seed there is no path that releases a reservation for a job that never launched. The job name is therefore retired and the two authorised runs below use new identities.

root_cause_fixed_before_this_record: The $400 campaign cap was hardcoded in the launchers while aws/budget.py carried the owner-amended $5000 cap. CAMPAIGN_CAP_USD now derives from budget.CAP.

validate_state demanded that EVERY write-ahead history entry carry today's cap, so after the cap raise all 70 entries failed and every paid launch was refused. Each state is now validated against the cap it recorded; only the operating head must carry the current cap, and only the head is compared to CAP.

The head/tail equality check and the write-ahead chain digest both require the ledger head and the newest history entry to be the same bytes. The cap amendment had edited the revision-69 head in place while history/00000069.json kept the pre-raise bytes, so the chain could not close. The amended revision-69 state was reconstructed and verified by reproducing the digest that revision 70 had already committed to: 9ac9970d319e2bb8b55c2154c9968703ddf0c864402196026d6ec0e3488b30cb. No reservation was altered.
The pre-raise bytes of revision 69 are preserved byte-for-byte in records/budget/PRESERVED_history_00000069_pre_cap_raise.json and records/budget/campaign_ledger.json.pre_cap_raise_400_to_5000.

instruction_interpretation: The owner directs that a real AWS GPU training run be executed and its results returned, so that the project can see what it actually has and plan from evidence rather than from design documents. Applied to CAS_RDCJT_001, this authorises TWO paired runs, one per never-launched seed, 20260913 and 20260914, at $7.00 each, $14.00 in total. Each job trains BOTH arms - one_pass and recurrent - from one matched initialization on the same CFC course, then reads the recurrent checkpoint at every declared depth with its weights frozen.

seed_accounting.measured_finding: All three earlier CAS_RDCJT_001 launches bound seed 20260912. Seeds 20260913 and 20260914 have never been launched.
seed_accounting.seed_20260912_is_done: Seed 20260912 has one delivered measurement, R1=117 against R8=101, net -16, recovered under rescued_evidence/. It is NOT re-run.
seed_accounting.criterion: A positive R8-minus-R1 difference in at least two of three paired runs. Three paired runs exist only after both jobs below deliver.

budget_context.note: The reservation is a deliberately pessimistic ceiling, not a price. The recorded actual AWS charge for the whole 2026-09-12 working day was $1.68 against a $7.00-per-job reservation.
